Rashi on Pesachim 13a:10:1.hebrew: מאי לאו אפי' לאכול - בכל דבריו קבעו כמותו, ואף במה שקבע זמן האכילה עד ד' שעות, ואפילו בתרומה:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:10:1.english: What, is it not even to eat - In all of his statements they established [the halakha] in accordance with him, and even in that which he established the time of eating [as being] until four hours, and even with regard to teruma.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:10:2.hebrew: לא לבער - הא דקבעו כמותו, לא איירי באכילה אלא בביעור — שהיו חביריו חלוקין עליו שלא יבערו טהורות עד למחר, קבעו דשורפין מערב שבת בשלשה עשר. אבל בשיור, לעולם אימא לך: כדי לאכול עד חמש שעות, והיא בכלל:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:10:2.english: No, [only] to remove - That which they established [the halakha] in accordance with his opinion does not deal with eating, but [only] with removal — for [where] his colleagues disagreed with him, [holding] that they should not burn pure [teruma] until the morrow, they established that one burns [it] on the eve of Shabbat, on the thirteenth [of Nisan]. But regarding leaving over [food], one could always say to you: [one leaves over] enough to eat until five hours, and it [pure teruma] is included.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:11:1.hebrew: דיסקייא - שתי מלות מורכבות: שני שקים, אמתחת של עור:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:11:1.english: A saddlebag [disakkayya] - [It is] two words compounded: two sacks, a leather bag.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:11:2.hebrew: ונקבוה עכברים - והיה נחסר, וארבעה עשר בניסן היה, וחמץ בזול, ובא לפני רבי לידע אם ימכרוהו מפני חסרונו של מפקיד:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:11:2.english: And mice bore a hole in it - And [its contents] were diminishing, and it was the fourteenth of Nisan, and leaven was [selling] cheaply; and he came before Rabbi to know whether he should sell it on account of the depositor's loss.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:11:3.english: Wait - Lest its owner come and eat [it].

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:11:4.english: [In the] fifth [hour] - For from now on, he can no longer eat it.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:11:5.english: He said to him: Go and sell them in the market - While it is still permitted to derive benefit [from it].

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:12:1.hebrew: לא לישראל - וכר' מאיר, והכי קאמר ליה: אי שהייתו הא שעתא, לא משכחת ישראל דזבין ליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:12:1.english: No, to an Israelite - And [this is] in accordance with Rabbi Meir, and this is what he said to him: If you delay [past] this hour, you will not find an Israelite who will buy it.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:12:2.hebrew: נישקליה לנפשיה - ויאכלנו, ויתן דמין לבעלים. למה לו לטרוח ולילך בשוק, אחרי שנותן לו רשות למכור:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:12:2.english: Let him take it for himself - And eat it, and give the money to the owner. Why should he trouble himself to go to the marketplace, since he is giving him permission to sell?

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:13:1.hebrew: פורטין - פרוטות של נחשת שגבו לצדקה, וכשמשהין אותם מחלידות — צריך לפורטן בכסף:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:13:1.english: They change - [Copper] perutot that they collected for charity, and when one keeps them they rust — [so] one must change them for silver [coins].

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:14:1.hebrew: תמחוי - מאכל — לחם ומיני מאכל שגובין לחלק:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:14:1.english: Charity plate - Food — bread and types of food that they collect to distribute.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:14:2.english: And do not sell to themselves - Lest [people] suspect them of having bought them cheaply.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:15:1.hebrew: בפירוש אמרת לן כו' - רב יוסף חלה ושכח תלמודו, ולאחר זמן, כשהיה מחליף דבריו, היו מזכירין אותו תלמידיו: "כך לימדתנו בראשונה":
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:15:1.english: You told us explicitly, etc. - Rav Yosef fell ill and forgot his learning, and later on, when he would change his words, his students would remind him: "Thus you taught us initially."

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:16:1.english: In accordance with whom does this [ruling] of Rabbi go - That he instructed to sell a deposit because it would be lost.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:2:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - That one suspends [it] all of the fifth [hour].

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:2:2.hebrew: ונימא הלכה כר' מאיר - דאוכלין כל חמש, דהא סתם לן תנא כוותיה. דתנן: "כל שעה שמותר לאכול — מאכיל לבהמה, לחיה, ולעופות", דמשמע: כשאינו מותר לאכול — אינו מאכיל. ואי רבי יהודה — הא איכא חמש, דאינו אוכל ומאכיל! אלא ר' מאיר היא, דאמר: אוכל עד תחלת שש, ומשעה שאינו אוכל — אין מאכיל:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:2:2.english: And let us say the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Meir - That one may eat during the entire fifth [hour], for the Tanna taught an unattributed [Mishnah] in accordance with his opinion. As we learned: “Any time that it is permitted to eat, one may feed [it] to domestic animals, to wild beasts, and to birds,” which implies [that] when it is not permitted to eat, one may not feed [it]. And if [the Mishnah is according to] Rabbi Yehuda, behold, there is the fifth [hour], when one does not eat, yet one may feed [it]! Rather, it is [according to] Rabbi Meir, who says [that] one may eat until the beginning of the sixth [hour], and from the time that one does not eat, one may not feed [it].

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:4:1.hebrew: משום דקשיא מותר - בפרק כל שעה מקשינן: ״כל שעה שאוכל מאכיל״ מיבעי ליה, ו״מותר״ משמע: כל שעה שמותר אדם אחר לאכול, מאכיל זה האסור לאכול. ומדוחקא דהא קושיא אוקימנא כרבן גמליאל, והכי קאמר: כל שעה שמותר כהן לאכול בתרומה, מאכיל ישראל חולין לבהמה. אלמא, סתמא לא כר"מ היא:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:4:1.english: Because "permitted" is difficult - In the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah, we raise an objection: It should have [stated], "All the time that one eats, he may feed"; and "permitted" implies: All the time that another person is permitted to eat, this [person who is] forbidden to eat may feed [it to animals]. And due to the difficulty of this objection, we established [that mishna] in accordance with [the view of] Rabban Gamliel; and this is what it means: All the time that a priest is permitted to eat terumah, an Israelite may feed non-sacred [food] to animals. Consequently, the unattributed [mishna] is not in accordance with Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:5:1.english: In accordance with Rabban Gamliel - As stated in the Mishnah:

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:5:2.hebrew: לאו מכריע הוא - כדפרישית לקמן בפירקין (פסחים ד' כא.), דאין הכרעת דעת שלישית מכרעת. והא הכרעת דעת שלישית היא, דהא ר"מ ורבי יהודה לא איירי דניהוי שייך חילוק בין זמן תרומה לזמן חולין כלל. דאי הוה תנן: ר"מ אומר אחד חולין וא' תרומה כל חמש; ר' יהודה אומר א' חולין ואחד תרומה כל ארבע; ורבן גמליאל אומר חולין כל ארבע, תרומה כל חמש — הויא הכרעה. אבל השתא, דאינהו לא אדכור תרומה וחולין כלל, ולא גלו דעתם שיהא שום רמז דין לחלק ביניהם — לאו הכרעה היא, אלא דעת שלישית:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:5:2.english: He is not a decisor - As I explained later in our chapter (Pesachim 21a), that the compromise of a third opinion is not decisive. And this [ruling] is the compromise of a third opinion, for Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda did not discuss [the matter in a way] that there would be any distinction between the time of teruma and the time of non-sacred food at all. For had we learned [in the Mishnah]: Rabbi Meir says: Both non-sacred food and teruma [may be eaten] throughout five [hours]; Rabbi Yehuda says: Both non-sacred food and teruma [may be eaten] throughout four [hours]; and Rabban Gamliel says: Non-sacred food throughout four [hours], teruma throughout five [hours] — [then] it would be a [valid] compromise. But now that they did not mention teruma and non-sacred food at all, and did not reveal their view that there is any basis in law to distinguish between them, it is not a compromise, but rather a third opinion.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:6:1.hebrew: ה"ג ואיבעית אימא רב דאמר כי האי תנא - דקבע הלכתא כר' אלעזר בר' יהודה, דאמר: אפי' תרומה כל ארבע ותו לא, דקתני דקבעו הלכה כמותו:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:6:1.english: This is the reading: “And if you wish, say: Rav, who said [this, ruled] in accordance with this tanna” - For [Rav] established the halakha in accordance with Rabbi Elazar ben Yehuda, who said: Even teruma [may only be eaten] all four [hours] and no more, as [the baraita] teaches that they established the halakha in accordance with his opinion.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:6:2.english: In abeyance - [Of] uncertain impurity [and] uncertain purity.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:6:3.hebrew: מזון שתי סעודות - ולא שלש, דכל שלש סעודות דשבת — ערבית, שחרית ומנחה — וערב פסח אסור לאכול מן המנחה ולמעלה:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:6:3.english: Food for two meals - And not three [meals], for all three meals of Shabbat [are] — evening, morning, and afternoon [minḥa] — and on the eve of Passover it is forbidden to eat from minḥa [time] onward.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:7:1.hebrew: טהורות לא ישרפו - כלל, הואיל ולא הגיע זמנן לבער. ואע"פ שיש לו שיור כדי לאנשי ביתו של כהן, שמא ימצא כהנים אורחים שיאכילום, ולא נפסיד תרומה בידים. ואם לא ימצא, יאכילום למחר לכלבי כהנים, או יבטלם בלבו:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:7:1.english: Pure [teruma] shall not be burned - At all, since the time for their removal has not [yet] arrived. And even though he has a reserve sufficient for the members of the priest's household, perhaps he will find guest priests whom he can feed them, and we will not actively destroy teruma. And if he does not find [any], he can feed them tomorrow to priests' dogs, or nullify them in his heart.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:7:2.hebrew: כבר בקשו ולא מצאו - כלומר, כל מה שיש לו לבקש כבר ביקש, דהא בשבת לא יבואו אורחים, וכבר יודע ובקי הוא באותן שבעיר מי יבוא אצלו:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:7:2.english: They already sought and did not find - That is to say, whatever he has to seek out, he has already sought out, for on Shabbat guests will not arrive, and he already knows and is familiar with those [who are] in the city [regarding] who will come to him.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:7:3.hebrew: לנו - לשון מלון: שמא בתוך התחום לנים כהנים אורחים הלילה, ויבואו למחר:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:7:3.english: They lodged - An expression of lodging: perhaps visiting priests are lodging within the [Shabbat] boundary tonight, and they will come tomorrow.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:8:1.hebrew: אף לדבריכם - דחיישינן לשמא, אמאי לא פלגיתו אלא בטהורות? אף תלויות לא ישרפו קודם זמנן, שמא יבוא אליהו היום או מחר קודם זמן ביעורן ויטהרם, ויאמר: "לא נגע בהן טומאה", ויאכלום:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:8:1.english: Even according to your statement - [Since] we are concerned for a "perhaps," why do you disagree only regarding pure [teruma]? Even [teruma] in abeyance should not be burned before its time, lest Elijah come today or tomorrow, before the time of its destruction, and declare it pure, and say: "Defilement did not touch it," and [the priests] will eat it.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:8:2.hebrew: לא בערבי שבתות כו' - והיום ערב שבת, ולמחר ערב יום טוב:
Rashi on Pesachim 13a:8:2.english: Neither on Shabbat eves, etc. - And today is the eve of Shabbat, and tomorrow is the eve of the Festival.

Rashi on Pesachim 13a:8:3.english: Due to the exertion - For they have to occupy themselves with the Shabbat meals, and they would be preoccupied with it.

Tosafot on Pesachim 13a:12:1.hebrew: מאי לאו לנכרים - להכי משמע לנכרים, דאי לישראל — לישקול לנפשיה, כדפריך אביי בסמוך. בירושלמי גרס: "צא ומוכרה בבית דין בשוק". משמע: אע"פ שנתן לו רשות רבי, שהיה אב"ד, למכור — אפי' הכי צריך ב"ד בשעת מכירה כדי לשומן. וא"ת: מ"ש מאלמנה, דמוכרת לאחרים שלא בב"ד, ובב"ד יכולה לעכב אפילו לעצמה? דאמר בכתובות (ד' צח. ושם): "אלמנה ששמה לעצמה — לא עשתה ולא כלום, דאמר: מאן שם ליך?", משמע דבבית דין יכולה לשום! וקאמרינן נמי התם: "ההוא גברא דאפקידו גביה כיסתא דיתמי, אזל שמה לנפשיה, לסוף אייקר; אמר ליה: מאן שם ליך?" וי"ל: דמוכרת שלא בבית דין — משום חינא. וגבי כיסתא דיתמי, דיכול לעכב לעצמו — היינו דוקא בדיעבד. א"נ: גבי יתמי, בית דין עצמן הן המפקידים, ולכך יכול לעכב לעצמו על פיהם; אבל פקדון של אחרים — לא. והא דאמר באלו מציאות (ב"מ כח:): "שם דמיהם ומניחן" גבי מציאה — התם ליכא חשד, שהרי הוא מחזיר אבידה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 13a:12:1.english: "What, is it not to gentiles" - It implies [that he meant] to gentiles for this reason: because if [he meant] to a Jew, let him take it for himself, as Abaye challenges immediately afterward. In the Yerushalmi the text reads: "Go out and sell it in a Beit Din in the market." This implies that even though Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who was the Av Beit Din, gave him permission to sell, even so he needs a Beit Din at the time of the sale in order to appraise them. And if you should say: How is [this] different from a widow, who sells [estate property] to others without a Beit Din, and in a Beit Din she can even retain [it] for herself? For [the Gemara] says in Ketubot (98a and there): "A widow who appraised [the property] for herself has done nothing, for [the heirs may] say: 'Who appraised it for you?'" — which implies that in a Beit Din she can appraise [and retain it]. And we also say there: [There was] a certain man with whom [people] deposited coral belonging to orphans; he went and appraised it for himself, and in the end it appreciated in value; [the judge] said to him: "Who appraised it for you?" And one can say: That [a widow] sells without a Beit Din is for the sake of grace [mishum ḥina, to ensure marriageability]. And regarding the coral of orphans, where he can retain [it] for himself, that is specifically after the fact. Alternatively, regarding orphans, the Beit Din themselves are considered the depositors, and therefore he can retain [it] for himself based on their authority; but with a deposit belonging to others, no. And as for that which [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] Elu Metzi'ot (Bava Metzia 28b): "He assesses their value and sets it aside" regarding a lost object — there, there is no suspicion, for he is returning a lost object.

Tosafot on Pesachim 13a:5:1.hebrew: רבן גמליאל לאו מכריע הוא - וקשה לר"י: דלימא הלכה כר"ג, דסתם לן תנא כוותיה בפ' כל שעה (לקמן פסחים כא.) מדקתני "מותר"! ואפי' אם מספקא ליה אם יש לדקדק בלשון "מותר" אם לאו — מ"מ נימא הלכה כר' מאיר או כרבן גמליאל, דממה נפשך ההיא דכל שעה כחד מינייהו אתו? וי"ל, דאאיבעית אימא סמיך. ודין הכרעה אפרש בסוף פירקין בע"ה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 13a:5:1.english: "Rabban Gamliel is not a decisor" - And the Ri raises a difficulty: For let him say that the halakha is in accordance with Rabban Gamliel, as the tanna taught an unattributed [mishna] in accordance with his opinion in the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah (below, Pesachim 21a), from the fact that it teaches "permitted"! And even if he is in doubt whether one should infer from the phrasing "permitted" or not — nevertheless, let us say that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Meir or in accordance with Rabban Gamliel, for one way or the other, that [mishna] of Kol Sha'ah follows one of them! And it can be said that he relies on the "if you wish, say" [alternative explanation that follows]. And the law of a compromise [ruling] I will explain at the end of our chapter, with God's help.

Tosafot on Pesachim 13a:6:1.hebrew: ושורפין תרומות טמאות ותלויות וטהורות - אפילו אם נאמר דאסור לשרוף טהורות משום דכתיב (במדבר י״ח:ח׳): "את משמרת תרומותי", כמו שאסור לטמאם — הכא שרי. אע"ג דמדאורייתא בביטול בעלמא סגי ואין צריך לשורפה, מכל מקום כיון דסופה ליאסר ולילך לאיבוד — שרי לשורפה; כמו לטמאותה, דשרי ר' מאיר בסוף פירקין לשרוף טמאה עם הטהורה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 13a:6:1.english: "And one burns ritually impure terumot, in abeyance, and pure" - Even if we say that it is forbidden to burn pure [terumah] because it is written: "The charge of My terumot" (Numbers 18:8), just as it is forbidden to defile them — here it is permitted. Even though by Torah law mere nullification is sufficient and there is no need to burn it, nevertheless, since it will ultimately become forbidden and go to waste, it is permitted to burn it — just like rendering it impure, which Rabbi Meir permits at the end of our chapter: to burn impure [terumah] together with pure [terumah].

Tosafot on Pesachim 13a:6:2.hebrew: ומשיירין מזון שתי סעודות - וכ"ש בחולין, שאוכליהן מרובין, דמשיירין, כדמשמע בתוספת':
Tosafot on Pesachim 13a:6:2.english: "And one leaves food for two meals" - And all the more so regarding non-sacred food [chullin], whose eaters are numerous, that one leaves [it over], as is implied in the Tosefta.
